entity_title: Register residence within 30 days after the first 3 months
fact_text: An EU citizen staying in Slovakia longer than three months must apply to register their residence, in person on the official form at a (foreign) police department. The application must be filed within 30 days of the day the first three months from entry elapse.
evidence_quote: Občan Únie, ktorý sa zdržiava na území Slovenskej republiky dlhšie ako tri mesiace, je povinný požiadať o registráciu pobytu na území Slovenskej republiky. Žiadosť o registráciu pobytu sa podáva na úradnom tlačive osobne na policajnom útvare do 30 dní od uplynutia troch mesiacov odo dňa vstupu na územie Slovenskej republiky.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Free movement still means paperwork: the clock is 30 days after the 3-month mark (not 30 days from arrival), and registration is a personal, in-person act on the official form at the foreign police.

entity_title: Report your stay to the foreign police within 10 working days of entry
fact_text: Separately from the >3-month residence registration, a Union citizen and their family member must report the start and place of their stay within 10 working days of entering Slovakia. In hotels/accommodation facilities the provider files it; in private accommodation the individual must file it at the foreign police department for their address.
evidence_quote: občan Únie a rodinný príslušník občana Únie: do 10 pracovných dní od vstupu na územie Slovenskej republiky

applies_to.non_obvious_note: This 10-working-day 'hlasenie pobytu' is an earlier, separate obligation from the >3-month registration; most EU movers do not realise reporting their address is required, and in private housing the duty falls on them, not a landlord.

entity_title: A national ID card is enough for registration; no passport needed
fact_text: To register, an EU citizen presents one identity document: a valid travel document, OR a valid identity card, OR any other credible document proving identity and nationality (e.g. a driving licence together with a birth certificate). A separate proof of the purpose of stay is also required.
evidence_quote: K žiadosti je povinný predložiť jeden z týchto dokladov: platný cestovný doklad alebo platný preukaz totožnosti akýkoľvek iný hodnoverný doklad preukazujúci totožnosť a štátnu príslušnosť (napr. vodičský preukaz spolu s rodným listom)

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A national ID card suffices (no passport needed), and Slovakia explicitly accepts a driving licence plus birth certificate as identity proof.

entity_title: Employment is proven by an employer letter, not a work permit
fact_text: When an employed EU citizen registers residence, the purpose of stay is proven by the employer's promise of employment or a confirmation of hiring. No work permit is involved — the employer letter is the qualifying document.
evidence_quote: a) Zamestnanie - prísľub zamestnávateľa alebo potvrdenie zamestnávateľa o prijatí do zamestnania.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: EU residence registration is purpose-based; employed movers qualify via an employer letter (promise/confirmation of hiring), which distinguishes them from self-sufficient movers who must instead show funds and health insurance.

entity_title: Registration confirmation is issued the same day
fact_text: On the day a complete registration application is filed, the police department issues the EU citizen a confirmation of residence registration stating name, surname, address and the date of registration.
evidence_quote: Policajný útvar vydá občanovi Únie v deň podania úplnej žiadosti o registráciu potvrdenie o registrácii pobytu občana Únie, v ktorom uvedie meno, priezvisko, adresu registrovanej osoby a dátum registrácie.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The confirmation is issued immediately on the day of a complete application (no waiting period), so a complete file yields documented proof of residence the same day.

entity_title: Optional EU residence card, valid five years
fact_text: After the right of residence is registered, an EU citizen may optionally ask the police for a residence document called 'Pobytovy preukaz obcana EU', valid for five years and issued within 30 days. The card requires a proof of accommodation and one 3x3.5 cm photo and carries an administrative fee.
evidence_quote: Občan Únie podľa § 65 ods. 1, ktorému policajný útvar zaregistroval právo na pobyt môže požiadať policajný útvar o vydanie dokladu o pobyte s názvom "Pobytový preukaz občana EÚ" s platnosťou na päť rokov. Policajný útvar vydá občanovi Únie doklad o pobyte do 30 dní.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The legal right of residence comes from the registration itself; the plastic card is optional and separate. Its validity is five years (some guides wrongly state ten).

entity_title: You get a registration certificate, not a residence permit
fact_text: As an EU national you are not issued a third-country-style residence permit; registering produces a registration certificate that confirms your existing right of residence. It should be issued immediately and cost no more than the price nationals pay for their identity cards.
evidence_quote: Your registration certificate should be issued immediately and cost no more than the price nationals pay for identity cards.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR teams used to third-country permits over-plan here: an EU mover's document is a cheap certificate of a pre-existing right, not a discretionary permit.

entity_title: Late registration is fineable but never grounds for expulsion
fact_text: If you were required to register and did not, you may be fined, but you may continue to live in the country and cannot be expelled just for failing to register.
evidence_quote: If you are required to register, you may be fined for not doing so but may continue to live in the country and cannot be expelled just for this.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Missing Slovakia's 30-day registration deadline exposes you to a fine but never to expulsion — a proportionality safeguard under EU free-movement law.

entity_title: A home available, or 183 days, makes you a Slovak tax resident
fact_text: You become a Slovak tax resident (person with unlimited tax liability) if you have permanent residence, a dwelling/domicile ('bydlisko') available to you, or you usually stay in Slovakia at least 183 days in the calendar year. It is not based on citizenship.
evidence_quote: Rezident SR (daňovník s neobmedzenou daňovou povinnosťou) – podľa § 2 písm. d) zákona o dani z príjmov je na účely tohto zákona fyzická osoba, ktorá má na území SR trvalý pobyt, bydlisko alebo sa tu obvykle zdržiava aspoň 183 dní v príslušnom kalendárnom roku a tiež právnická osoba, ktorá má na území SR sídlo alebo miesto skutočného vedenia.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Having a home available in Slovakia ('bydlisko') can make you tax-resident even under 183 days, so an EU professional who rents a flat can trigger residency early.

entity_title: Slovak tax residents are taxed on worldwide income
fact_text: A Slovak tax resident's taxable income covers income from sources in Slovakia AND from sources abroad — so-called worldwide income (subject to double-tax treaties).
evidence_quote: Predmet dane rezidenta SR – je podľa § 2 písm. f) zákona o dani z príjmov príjem (výnos) plynúci zo zdrojov na území SR a zo zdrojov v zahraničí (tzv. celosvetový príjem).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Once resident, foreign rental income, dividends or other foreign-source income become reportable in Slovakia (treaty relief applies), not just the Slovak salary.

entity_title: Employer must register you with Socialna poistovna before day one
fact_text: The employer must register a new employee with the Social Insurance Agency (Socialna poistovna) at the latest before they start work — this applies to non-Slovak, including EU, employees too.
evidence_quote: Employees need to be registered at the latest before they start work.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Social-insurance registration is the employer's duty and must be completed before the first working day, not after onboarding; a late registration is an employer compliance failure.

entity_title: The Interior Ministry assigns a birth number (rodne cislo) to residents
fact_text: Slovak administration runs on the rodne cislo (birth number). The Ministry of Interior assigns a rodne cislo to a foreigner — including an EU citizen granted residence — who has residence (permanent, temporary or tolerated) in Slovakia and does not yet have one.
evidence_quote: c) cudzincovi, ktorému doteraz nebolo pridelené a ktorý má trvalý pobyt, prechodný pobyt, tolerovaný pobyt, alebo ktorý na území Slovenskej republiky požíva výsady a imunity podľa medzinárodného práva a je akreditovaný Ministerstvom zahraničných vecí a európskych záležitostí Slovenskej republiky,

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The rodne cislo underpins banking, e-government (eID), health and payroll; EU citizens obtain it through their residence registration. The statute (Act 301/1995 § 5) lists it as assigned to foreigners with pobyt who lack one.

entity_title: No birth number yet? The employer's SIA form still registers you
fact_text: The birth number doubles as the social-security identification number. A foreigner working in Slovakia for the first time who has neither a birth number nor a social-security identification number is still registered: the employer files the Natural Person Registration Form (RFLO) with the Social Insurance Agency.
evidence_quote: In the case of a foreigner who is working in the Slovak Republic for the first time (does not have a birth number or a social security identification number), the employer can send to the relevant branch of the Social Insurance Agency a Natural Person Registration Form - application electronically via eServices or in paper form.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A newly-arrived EU worker without a rodne cislo is not blocked from social insurance — the employer's RFLO filing obtains the identifier; the birth number, once assigned, serves as the social-security ID.

entity_title: Pick one health fund and file within 8 days — you cannot be uninsured
fact_text: Public health insurance is mandatory and is triggered by events such as becoming an employee or moving your residence from another EU member state to Slovakia. The insured person must file a registration form (prihlaska) with a health insurance company within eight days of the triggering event, and may register with only one fund (VsZP, Dovera or Union).
evidence_quote: Poistenec je povinný podať prihlášku na verejné zdravotné poistenie v zdravotnej poisťovni do ôsmich dní odo dňa vzniku skutočnosti zakladajúcej vznik verejného zdravotného poistenia

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Distinct from the employer's social-insurance registration, the employee must personally file the health-insurance prihlaska within 8 days and choose a single fund; you cannot lawfully be uninsured while resident/employed.

entity_title: You can register residence without a lease — only the municipality is recorded
fact_text: If an EU citizen does not submit an accommodation document (per § 122), the police still register them but record only the municipality (obec) where they will stay as the address on the registration confirmation. A formal accommodation document is, however, required later to obtain the EU residence card.
evidence_quote: Ak občan Únie nepredloží doklad podľa § 122, policajný útvar uvedie ako adresu v potvrdení o registrácii obec, kde sa občan Únie bude zdržiavať na pobyte.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A common blocker — 'I have no lease yet' — does not stop residence registration: the police record just the municipality. The accommodation document (doklad o ubytovani § 122) becomes necessary only for the plastic residence card.
